title: see somebody do and see somebody doing
subtitle: I saw him do / I saw him doing
summary: Use see somebody do for a complete action you saw from start to finish, and see somebody doing for an action in progress.

lesson.heading: I saw him do something
lesson.text: Tom got into his car and drove off, and you saw this. You can say: **I saw Tom get into his car and drive off.** We say 'I saw him **do** something' = he did it and I saw this.

examples.note: = you came in and I didn't hear this

examples.text: Lisa suddenly felt somebody **touch** her on the shoulder.

lesson.heading: I saw her doing something
lesson.text: Yesterday you saw Kate. She was waiting for a bus. You can say: **I saw Kate waiting for a bus.** We say 'I saw her **doing** something' = she was doing it and I saw this. You can use *see, hear, listen to, watch, feel, smell* and *find* in this way.

examples.note: = it was raining and I could hear it

examples.text: We looked for Paul and finally we found him **sitting** under a tree **eating** an apple.

left.label: I saw him do something
left.text: He did something and I saw this. I saw the complete action from start to finish.
examples: He jumped over the wall and ran away. I saw this. -> I saw him **jump** over the wall and **run** away.
They went out. I heard this. -> I heard them **go** out.

right.label: I saw him doing something
right.text: He was doing something and I saw this. I saw him in the middle of doing it, not from start to finish.
examples: I saw Tom as I drove past. He was walking along the street. -> I saw Tom **walking** along the street.
I heard them. They were talking. -> I heard them **talking**.

lesson.heading: When either form is possible
lesson.text: Sometimes the difference is not important and you can use either form.

examples.text: I've never seen her **dance**. *or* I've never seen her **dancing**.

lesson.text: After see, hear, watch and feel we never use to: say *I saw him go out*, not ~~I saw him to go out~~.

exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't have the keys. I saw him ___ them to Lisa.
exercises.explanation: After see + object we use the infinitive without to: I saw him give them to Lisa.

exercises.prompt: We heard a car ___ outside our house, and then it drove off again.
exercises.explanation: We heard the complete action, so: heard a car stop.

exercises.prompt: Ben gave me the envelope and watched me ___ it.
exercises.explanation: He watched the whole action from start to finish: watched me open it.

exercises.statement: Sarah is Canadian. I heard her say she's from Toronto.
exercises.explanation: Correct. hear somebody say something = the complete thing was said and I heard it.

exercises.statement: We saw a man fell over in the street, so we went to help him.
exercises.explanation: We saw a man fall over in the street. After see + object we use the infinitive without to, not a past form.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday we passed the bus stop. Kate was standing there. We saw Kate ___ for a bus.
exercises.explanation: She was in the middle of waiting, so: saw Kate waiting.

exercises.prompt: There was a strange smell in the kitchen. We could smell something ___.
exercises.explanation: Something was burning at that moment: smell something + -ing.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Can you hear a baby ___?
exercises.explanation: The baby is in the middle of crying: hear somebody + -ing.

exercises.prompt: Everybody heard the bomb ___. It was a tremendous noise.
exercises.explanation: The explosion was one complete action: heard the bomb explode.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: We looked for Paul and finally we found him sitting under a tree eating an apple.
exercises.explanation: find somebody + -ing: he was in the middle of sitting and eating when we found him.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

pairs.left: I looked out of the window and saw Dan
pairs.right: riding his bike along the road.
slam a door in the middle of the night.

pairs.left: When I got home, I found a cat

pairs.right: crawling up my leg. It must be an insect.

pairs.left: We listened to the old man
pairs.right: tell his story from beginning to end.

pairs.left: There was an accident outside my house, but I didn't see it

exercises.prompt: Did the speaker see or hear the complete action, or only the middle of it?

items.text: I saw him jump over the wall and run away.
I saw Tom walking along the street.
I didn't hear you come in.
